T1: #### T1: `pending -> published`, the pipeline's write-back (ADR-0121) For an index `i < n`, `new.versions[i]` is permitted to differ from `old.versions[i]` under T1 if, and only if, all of the following hold: 1. `old.versions[i].status == "pending"` and `new.versions[i].status == "published"`. 2. `version`, `commit` and `source_url` are deep-equal to the old values: the fields the author supplied are frozen. 3. Each of `source_archive`, `source_sha256`, `signature`, `key_id` and `published_at` is present in `new.versions[i]`, absent from `old.versions[i]`, and satisfies its pattern (or, for `signature` and `key_id`, its minimum length) in `entry.schema.json`. 4. `new.versions[i]` has exactly the nine keys of the `published` row of the shape table, so no key outside them, and in particular no `reason` and no `build_log_url`. 5. The array is otherwise untouched: rules 1 to 3 and "Ordering of `versions[]`" apply to every other element. T1 happens exactly once, by structure: it requires `old.versions[i].status == "pending"`, and a `pending` element has none of the five pipeline-written fields. After T1 the element is `published`, and a `published` element is covered by plain deep-equality under rule 1 (or by T2), so the five fields can never be written a second time. `published -> pending` and `pending -> pending` with any change are violations of rule 1. Nothing else changes under T1: `id` and `owner` stay frozen, `page.json` is not part of this document, and no element is added, removed or reordered. T1 is checked for shape only. This document cannot check that `source_sha256` is the hash of the archive or that `signature` verifies, because no checker built from it has the tarball or the key; that is the job of the verifiers of `signature-format.md`, the site's verification and the launcher. A wrong but well-formed write-back is also never corrected by rewriting (T1 happens once); the remedy is a new version or a takedown. Worked example — permitted T1. `old.versions[0]`: ```json { "version": "1.0.0", "commit": "aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa", "source_url": "https://github.com/example/mod", "status": "pending" } ``` `new.versions[0]` (same index; the author keys unchanged, five keys added, `status` changed): ```json { "version": "1.0.0", "commit": "aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa", "source_url": "https://github.com/example/mod", "source_archive": "https://cdn.worldofmodcraft.org/archives/example-mod-1.0.0.tar.gz", "source_sha256": "bbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbbb", "signature": "cccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccccc", "key_id": "platform-2026-01", "published_at": "2026-10-15T09:00:00Z", "status": "published" } ``` Worked counter-example. The same `new.versions[0]` with `commit` changed to `dddd…`, or with `source_sha256` missing, or with an extra `reason` key, is a violation: the author-supplied fields are frozen, all five pipeline-written fields are required, and the key set is exact.
T3: #### T3: `pending -> rejected`, a build that will never succeed (ADR-0121 Q-J) For an index `i < n`, `new.versions[i]` is permitted to differ from `old.versions[i]` under T3 if, and only if, all of the following hold: 1. `old.versions[i].status == "pending"` and `new.versions[i].status == "rejected"`. 2. `version`, `commit` and `source_url` are deep-equal to the old values. 3. `reason` is present in `new.versions[i]`, absent from `old.versions[i]`, a string, and non-empty after stripping leading and trailing whitespace; `build_log_url` is present in `new.versions[i]`, absent from `old.versions[i]`, and matches `^https://\S+$`. 4. `new.versions[i]` has exactly the keys of the `rejected` row of the shape table: none of the five pipeline-written fields of T1, and nothing else. 5. The array is otherwise untouched: rules 1 to 3 and "Ordering of `versions[]`" apply to every other element. `rejected` is terminal and one-way: `rejected -> anything` is a violation of rule 1, and so is `rejected -> rejected` with any change, `reason` included. A changed `reason` is not a correction mechanism; the fix for a failed build is a new version. A `rejected` element is never deleted (rule 3) and its `version` string stays occupied (rule 4). A `rejected` version is never installable or resolvable. T3 is checked for shape only, like T1: whether the build really failed, and whether `build_log_url` points at a true log, cannot be checked by this document. Consumers treat `pending` and `rejected` as not resolvable and say "exists but is not yet published" rather than "not found" (ADR-0121 Consequences); that behaviour belongs to the launcher, the site and the resolver and is recorded here only as a dependency. Worked example — permitted T3. `old.versions[1]`: ```json { "version": "1.1.0", "commit": "aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa", "source_url": "https://github.com/example/mod", "status": "pending" } ``` `new.versions[1]`: ```json { "version": "1.1.0", "commit": "aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa", "source_url": "https://github.com/example/mod", "status": "rejected", "reason": "Build failed: the manifest declares a dependency that does not exist.", "build_log_url": "https://builds.worldofmodcraft.org/logs/example-mod-1.1.0.txt" } ``` Worked counter-example. The same element with `reason` set to `" "`, or with `build_log_url` starting `http://`, or carrying a `signature` key, is a violation.
COEXISTENCE: #### Coexistence of T1, T2 and T3 - T1 and T3 start from `pending`, T2 starts from `published`, and each ends in a different state, so one element cannot undergo two of them in one PR. `pending -> removed` is a violation (nothing was archived, so there is nothing to pull), and so is `published -> rejected`. A T1 element carrying a `reason` or a `build_log_url` is a violation, and so is a T3 element carrying any of the five pipeline-written fields (the key sets above are exact). - Shape layer and authority layer. This document classifies each element independently. A PR holding a T1 on one version and a T2 or T3 on another is shape-legal. Who may carry which belongs to `ownership.md`: its `R11` takedown PR must contain nothing but takedown mutations, which excludes T1 and T3 in the same PR, and the pipeline's carve-out (a sibling task) must be keyed on the pipeline identity and on T1 or T3 mutations only. - Fail closed. Until `ownership.md` carries the pipeline-identity carve-out for T1 and T3, a checker implementing T1 or T3 must reject every PR that contains a T1 or T3 mutation, whoever authors it. Without this default an author could write their own `published` or `rejected` fields. - Authority for T1 and T3 is therefore not defined by this document. It defines the shape of the transitions, as the T2 section says of the takedown.
ATTACKS: #### Attack attempts the contract must answer 1. Author self-publishes. A PR appends a version already `published` with invented hashes. Answer: rule 2 and the shape table reject a born-`published` element. Were that rule absent, only `ownership.md` and the verification on install would stand between a forged object and users. 2. Garbage write-back by the pipeline identity. A compromised or buggy pipeline PR writes a well-formed but wrong `source_sha256`. This document cannot reject it, because T1 is shape only. The defences are the pipeline-identity carve-out keyed on "exactly T1", the fresh hash and signature verification on install (`signature-format.md`), and the fact that a wrong hash cannot be rewritten: the remedy is a new version or a takedown. This is a known limit, not a hidden one. 3. Splicing a takedown into the pipeline PR so a version vanishes unnoticed. Shape-legal per element, rejected at the authority layer (`R11` "nothing but takedown mutations"; the carve-out "exactly T1 or T3"). The tests belong to the sibling tasks; this document records the dependency. 4. Pending squatting. An author appends `pending` versions that will never build, burning version strings. Rule 4 makes the squat permanent; T3 turns each such version into a recorded, explained terminal state but does not prevent the squat (ADR-0121 Consequences). The cost falls on the squatter's own namespace. 5. Forged rejection. An author marks their own `pending` version `rejected` with a self-chosen reason, to skip the pipeline and retry the same string. Shape-legal here (T3 is shape only), rejected by the fail-closed rule and later by the ownership carve-out keyed on the pipeline identity; this is why that carve-out covers T3 as well as T1.
